Formulation
- Brief Summary: A new or subacute irritant contact dermatitis with secondary dryness and itching, likely related to occupational exposure to cleaning agents and inconsistent glove use after a recent job change. Skin symptoms are impacting work capacity. Appropriate management includes trigger avoidance (glove use), topical anti-inflammatory treatment, and intensified moisturization. Diabetes is present as a past medical history factor; no psychosocial risk factors identified in the transcript beyond occupational stressors.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Relieve dermatitis symptoms; return to full work duties; reduce exposure to irritants
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduction in skin inflammation and cracking; improved skin barrier; adherence to protective measures
- Actions (Patient): Wear gloves during cleaning at all times; apply emollients 3–4 times daily; use prescribed topical steroid as directed; follow up if not improved in 1–2 weeks; avoid known irritants
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe topical steroid cream (name not documented) and stronger emollients (name not documented); provide gloves-use guidance; schedule follow-up in 1–2 weeks; reinforce trigger-avoidance strategies
